name: Strategic Planning, Execution & Performance Management
description: Deterministic operating system framework to translate strategic vision into executable workstreams, milestones, tasks, KPIs, Balanced Scorecards, and executive dashboards.
logic: Most organizations do not fail because they lack strategy. They fail because strategy never becomes consistent execution. Every project must trace back to a strategic objective; measure outcomes, not activity.
chainsOfThought: Step 1: Initiate Strategic Planning -> Define Vision, Mission & Strategic Pillars -> Establish Annual Goals
Step 2: Initiative Decomposition -> Break Pillars into Strategic Initiatives, Programs & Workstreams -> Assign Executive Owners
Step 3: Project Architecture -> Translate Initiatives into Projects, Milestones, Tasks & Dependency Networks -> Calculate Critical Path
Step 4: Performance Architecture -> Define KPIs, Scorecards, Health Formulas & Target Metrics -> Map KPIs to Initiatives
Step 5: Resource & Capacity Allocation -> Evaluate Team Capacity, Budget & Skill Dependencies -> Mitigate Bottlenecks
Step 6: Risk & Dependency Audit -> Surface Hidden Dependencies & Execution Blockers -> Build Risk Register
Step 7: Health & Progress Calculation -> Run Formula (Expected = Elapsed / Planned) -> Assign Health States (On Track, At Risk, Overdue)
Step 8: Generate Executive Intelligence -> Synthesize Executive Dashboards, Scorecard Updates & Weekly Reports
Step 9: Human Review & Approval -> Request Executive Sign-Off via WebSocket -> Obtain Sign-Off on Scope, Priorities & Allocations
Step 10: Publish & Platform Sync -> Export to Notion, Airtable, CSV & Persistent Graph Memory -> Trigger Workflow Sync
bestPractices: Strategy before execution: work that does not advance strategy must be questioned before execution begins.
Health calculation must compare actual progress against elapsed time.
Require explicit human executive sign-off before triggering autonomous downstream deployment.
